items.definition:
iconic
The Eiffel Tower is an iconic landmark of Paris.

keen (eager, sharp)
She's very keen to learn new things.

mandatory
Wearing a helmet is mandatory for cyclists.

precise
We need precise measurements for this experiment.

protective
Parents are naturally protective of their children.

next to or adjoining something else
The library is adjacent to the park.

relating to elections or electors
The electoral system needs reform.

more than is necessary, normal, or desirable
The noise level was excessive.

arranged in or extending along a straight or nearly straight line
The story has a linear plot, moving from beginning to end.

not consistent or having a fixed pattern; liable to change
The weather in the mountains is highly variable.

occurring or succeeding by turns; every other
We meet on alternate Tuesdays.

relating to diplomacy; tactful
He gave a diplomatic answer to avoid offending anyone.

lasting or existing forever; without end
They swore eternal love to each other.

not specific; characteristic of a whole group or class
He bought the generic brand of cereal to save money.

having or showing a modest or low estimate of one's own importance
Despite his success, he remained a humble person.

enduring or permanent
Their friendship formed a lasting bond.

of a minimum amount, quantity, or degree
The damage to the car was minimal.

arousing pity, especially through vulnerability or sadness; miserably inadequate
His attempt to fix the car was pathetic.

showing signs of future success
She is a promising young artist.

savagely violent
The weather was brutal, with freezing winds and heavy snow.

causing death
The accident proved fatal for the driver.

featuring new methods, ideas, or products
The company is known for its innovative designs.

powerful, strong
The mighty river flowed through the valley.

relating to money or currency
The company faced significant monetary challenges.

having great influence
She is an influential figure in the art world.

having or showing strong feelings
She is passionate about her work.

having or showing a cautious distrust of someone or something
His behavior seemed very suspicious.

Favorable or advantageous.
Regular exercise is beneficial for your health.

Able to be compared.
The two products are comparable in quality.

magnificent; splendid
They celebrated a glorious victory.

certain to happen
Change is an inevitable part of life.

causing or characterized by extreme distress or sorrow
It was a tragic accident.

relating to or caused by a virus; circulated rapidly and widely on the internet
The video went viral overnight.

joined by agreement; related
The allied forces worked together to achieve their goal.

relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these
We must ensure that our business practices are ethical.

unfriendly; antagonistic
The crowd became hostile after the announcement.

nationwide
The company launched a nationwide advertising campaign.

notable
She made a notable contribution to the project.

optical
The optician checked his optical health.

petty
Don't argue over such petty matters.

tremendous
They made a tremendous effort to finish on time.

densely packed; small
The car was very compact, making it easy to park.

detailed and complicated in design or planning
She wore an elaborate dress to the party.

concentrated on a single area or subject
The course was very intensive, covering a lot of material.

closely acquainted; private and personal
They shared an intimate moment together.

of or appropriate to war; warlike
He practices martial arts every day.

based on or in accordance with reason or logic
Try to be rational about this decision.

beautiful in a dramatic and eye-catching way
The view from the mountain was spectacular.

relating to or involving technology
We live in a rapidly advancing technological age.

satisfactory or acceptable in quality or quantity
The food supply was adequate for everyone.

unusually good; outstanding
Her performance was truly exceptional.

unpleasant or disgusting; unfair
The air in the old building had a foul smell.

lacking knowledge or awareness in general; uneducated
Many people are ignorant of the true cost of living.

denoting or relating to the median of a set of values
The median age of the population is increasing.

relating to the Middle Ages
They visited a medieval castle in France.

complex, refined
The new software has a very sophisticated interface.

not moving or changing
The image on the screen remained static.

relating to surgery
The patient required surgical intervention.

genuine, real
This is an authentic antique vase.

impressively beautiful, elaborate, or extravagant; superb
The view from the mountain was magnificent.

relating to mathematics
He has a strong mathematical mind.

relating to heat
The house has excellent thermal insulation.

humble
She was very modest about her achievements.

not active
He took a passive role in the discussion.
